exercises.name: Lying Hamstring Stretch
exercises.note: Static holds like these belong AFTER training or on a rest day, never before you play. Held long enough to matter, they take a little edge off how forcefully a muscle contracts for the next hour or so. That is exactly what you want tonight and exactly what you do not want ten minutes before a match.

good: On your back, one leg up, hands behind the thigh, other leg flat on the floor
Soft bend in the raised knee. Straighter is not better
Relax into it. The hold does the work, not the pull
bad: Letting the other leg lift off the floor

good: On your back, ankle across the opposite knee, pull the bottom thigh in
Keep the crossed knee pushed gently away
Head and shoulders stay down
bad: Pulling so hard the hips lift off the floor

good: Soles of the feet together, sit tall, let the knees fall
Lean forward from the hips, not by rounding the back
Elbows can rest on the thighs. No pushing
bad: Rounding the spine to get lower

good: Back foot up on a sofa or wall, squeeze the back glute and stand tall
The glute squeeze is the stretch
bad: Arching the lower back to get deeper

good: Hands on the wall, back leg straight, heel down, hips forward
Then bend that back knee slightly and hold again. Two different muscles
Toes pointing straight at the wall the whole time
bad: Turning the back foot out to cheat the range

good: Forearm on the door frame, elbow at shoulder height, step through and turn away
Chest open, ribs down
bad: Letting the shoulder roll forward into the stretch
Going so far it pinches at the front of the shoulder. Back off if it does

good: From child's pose, walk both hands round to one side
Feel it down the side of the ribs and into the lat
bad: Letting the hips come off the heels

exercises.name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
exercises.note: The back of the serving shoulder takes a beating and it is the one nobody stretches. Gentle is the word here. If you feel a pinch at the front of the shoulder rather than a stretch behind it, come out and tell me.

good: Arm straight across the chest, pull it in with the other forearm
Keep the shoulder down, do not let it shrug up towards the ear
bad: Pulling at the elbow joint itself
Rotating the whole torso to make it feel like more
